The '''2018–19 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wolverines, led by head coach [[John Beilein]] in his twelfth year, played their home games for the 52nd consecutive year at the [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]. This season marked the program's 103rd season and its 102nd consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. They compiled a 30–7 overall record, 15–5 in the conference and finished in third place. In the Big Ten tournament, they defeated [[2018–19 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]] in the quarterfinals, [[2018–19 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] in the semifinals before losing to [[2018–19 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in the championship. They received a at-large bid to the NCAA tournament, defeating [[2018–19 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]] in the first round, [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the second round, but lost in the Sweet Sixteen to [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]].

==Previous season==
The Wolverines, who finished the 2017–18 season 33–8, were 13–5 in [[2017–18 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten play]] to finish in a tie for fourth. As the No. 5 seed in the [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]], [[2017–18 Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball team|Nebraska]], [[2017–18 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]], and [[2017–18 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] to win the tournament championship. As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As the No. 3 seed in the West region, they defeated [[2017–18 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]], [[2017–18 Houston Cougars men's basketball team|Houston]], [[2017–18 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], and [[2017–18 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]] to advance to the Final Four. In the National semifinal, they defeated [[2017–18 Loyola Ramblers men's basketball team|Loyola-Chicago]] before losing to [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]].

==Regular season==
The full schedule was announced on August 21. The marquee games are a home game against [[2018–19 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the [[ACC-Big Ten Challenge]] and a road game against [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/08/21/michigan-basketball-schedule-2018-here-all-games/1056339002/|title=Michigan basketball schedule 2018: All the games|access-date=August 24, 2018|date=August 21, 2018|work=[[Detroit Free Press]]|author=Sang, Orion}}</ref> The season will mark the first time in Big Ten history that the teams will play a 20-game conference schedule. During their next six-year cycle, teams within the same state will play 12 times, while teams within the same region will play 10 times. All other teams will play nine times. In addition, there will be three in-state series played between Illinois and Northwestern, Indiana and Purdue, and Michigan and Michigan State. Each time will play twice, guaranteeing a home game for each team.<ref name=":02">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/big-ten-adds-two-games-for-a-20-game-conference-schedule-starting-in-2018-19/|title=Big Ten adds two games for a 20-game conference schedule starting in 2018–19|last=Norlander|first=Matt|date=October 19, 2017|work=CBS Sports|access-date=March 9, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/21076233/big-ten-play-20-game-conference-schedule-next-season|title=Big Ten to move to 20-game conference slate|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-03-12}}</ref> The conference opponent list was finalized on April 19, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041918aae.html|title=2018–19 Conference Season Opponent Breakdown: Teams will compete in 20-game conference schedule, playing seven teams both home and away and six teams once|access-date=April 19, 2018|date=April 19, 2018|website=BigTen.org|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180420074326/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/041918aae.html|archive-date=April 20, 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 31, 2016, it was announced that Michigan would participate in the [[Hall of Fame Tip Off|2018 Hall of Fame Tip Off]] at the [[Mohegan Sun Arena]] in [[Uncasville, Connecticut]] on November 17 and 18.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2016/08/michigan_basketball_to_play_in_2.html|title=Michigan basketball to play in 2018 Hall of Fame Tip-Off|date=August 31, 2016|work=MLive.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}}</ref> On September 6, 2017, the three other participants for the tournament were announced: [[2018–19 George Washington Colonials men's basketball team|George Washington]], [[2018–19 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]], and [[2018–19 South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball team|South Carolina]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2017/09/report_george_washington_provi.html|title=Report: George Washington, Providence and South Carolina join Michigan in 2018 Hall of Fame Tip Off|date=September 6, 2017|work=MLive.com|access-date=April 7, 2018}}</ref>

===November===
Michigan began the season with a 63–44 victory over [[2018–19 Norfolk State Spartans men's basketball team|Norfolk State]]. Michigan was led by Jon Teske with a game-high 13 points, eight rebounds, and a then career-high four blocks, while freshman [[Ignas Brazdeikis]] scored 12 points in his Michigan debut. With the win, [[John Beilein]] earned his 800th career win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082446|title=Teske scores 13, No. 19 Michigan beats Norfolk State 63–44|access-date=November 6, 2018|date=November 6, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/11/6/mens-basketball-michigan-raises-banners-beilein-wins-800th-game-in-opening-night-victory.aspx?path=mbball|title=Michigan Raises Banners, Beilein Wins 800th Game in Opening Night Victory|access-date=November 7, 2018|date=November 7, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 10, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Holy Cross Crusaders men's basketball team|Holy Cross]] 56–37. Michigan was led by [[Charles Matthews (basketball)|Charles Matthews]] with a game-high 20 points, while Brazdeikis added 19 points, including 15 points in the first five minutes to start the second half. Teske added another five blocks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082447|title=Brazdeikis leads No. 19 Michigan over Holy Cross 56–37|access-date=November 10, 2018|date=November 10, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/11/10/mens-basketball-brazdeikis-second-half-performance-leads-michigan-to-victory-over-holy-cross.aspx?path=mbball|title=Brazdeikis' Second-Half Performance Leads Michigan to Victory over Holy Cross|access-date=November 10, 2018|date=November 10, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> On November 14, Michigan defeated (#8 [[AP Poll]]/#8 [[Coaches Poll]]) [[2018–19 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] 73–46 in the [[Gavitt Tipoff Games]]. Michigan was led by Matthews with a game-high 19 points, while Brazdeikis added 18 points, and a team-high seven rebounds. Michigan's defense forced 21 turnovers, including five steals by [[Zavier Simpson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082448|title=Michigan routs Villanova in championship rematch|access-date=November 14, 2018|date=November 14, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/11/14/mens-basketball-wolverines-run-out-early-cruise-to-victory-over-no-8-villanova.aspx|title=Wolverines Run Out Early, Cruise to Victory Over No. 8 Villanova|access-date=November 15, 2018|date=November 14, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On November 17, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 George Washington Colonials men's basketball team|George Washington]] 84–61. Michigan was led by Matthews with a game-high 25 points, while [[Jordan Poole]] added a then career-high 22 points, and Simpson added 14 points and 11 rebounds for his first career [[double-double]]. This marked the first time Michigan had two 20-point scorers in the same game since March 22, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082448|title=Michigan 84, George Washington 61|access-date=November 18, 2018|date=November 17, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/11/17/mens-basketball-pooles-career-high-simpsons-double-double-help-u-m-past-colonials.aspx|title=Poole's Career High, Simpson's Double-Double Help U-M Past Colonials|access-date=November 18, 2018|date=November 17, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> The next day Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] 66–47 to win the [[Hall of Fame Tip Off]] tournament. Michigan was led by Brazdeikis with a career-tying 20 points, while Teske added seven points and a career-high 12 rebounds.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082450|title=No. 9 Michigan rolls past Chattanooga 83–55|access-date=November 23, 2018|date=November 23, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/11/23/mens-basketball-wolverines-cruise-past-mocs-behind-career-highs-from-teske-brazdeikis.aspx|title=Wolverines Cruise Past Mocs Behind Career Highs from Teske, Brazdeikis|access-date=November 23, 2018|date=November 23, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On November 28, Michigan defeated (#11/#13) [[2018–19 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] 84–67 in the [[ACC–Big Ten Challenge]], as Michigan shot a season-high 57.4 percent from the field, and tied a season-best with 50-percent from three-point range. ===December===
On December 1, Michigan defeated (#19/#18) [[2018–19 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] 76–57 in its [[2018–19 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten Conference season]] opener. Michigan was led by Poole with a game-high 21 points, including 5-for-5 from three-point range, while Teske added a career-tying 17 points. Michigan's offense shot 50% on three point shots again and its defense held Purdue to 35.5% shooting, 26 points below their season average. Michigan's 19-point win marked the largest margin of victory over Purdue since [[1996–97 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1997]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082452|title=Poole scores 21, No. 7 Michigan beats No. 19 Purdue 86–57|access-date=December 1, 2018|date=December 1, 2018|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/12/1/mens-basketball-poole-defense-lead-u-m-past-no-19-18-purdue-to-eighth-consecutive-win.aspx|title=Poole, Defense Lead U-M Past No. 19/18 Purdue, to Eighth Consecutive Win|access-date=December 1, 2018|date=December 1, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On December 3, Poole was recognized as Big Ten Player of the Week and Brazdeikis was recognized as Big Ten Freshman of the Week for their performances against these two ranked teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/news/2018/12/3/michigan-sweeps-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181204005812/https://bigten.org/news/2018/12/3/michigan-sweeps-weekly-mens-basketball-honors.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 4, 2018|title=Michigan Sweeps Weekly Men's Basketball Honors|access-date=December 3, 2018|date=December 3, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2018/12/3/2018-19-michigan-mens-basketball-awards-and-honors.aspx|title=Awards & Honors: Poole, Brazdeikis Sweep B1G Weekly Honors|access-date=December 3, 2018|date=December 3, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref> On December 4, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] 62–60. Michigan was led by Brazdeikis with a game-high 23 points, his fourth 20-point game of the season. Michigan led by as many as 12 points late in the first half, however, Michigan State used a 20–2 run in the second half to take their first lead of the game, and eventually win the game. Michigan finished the season in third place, one game behind Michigan State and Purdue.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401082469|title=No. 9 Michigan State 75, No. 7 Michigan 63|access-date=March 9, 2019|date=March 9, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/9/mens-basketball-michigan-falls-to-michigan-state-in-regular-season-finale.aspx|title=Michigan Falls to Michigan State in Regular-Season Finale|access-date=March 9, 2019|date=March 9, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wyrot, Tom}}</ref>

==Postseason==
===Big Ten tournament===
On March 15, Michigan opened its [[2019 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]] play with a 74–53 victory over Iowa in the quarterfinals. Michigan was led by Brazdeikis with a game-high 15-points, while Teske added 12 points, 10 rebounds and two blocks for his eighth career double-double, and Simpson added 10 points and 11 assists for his fourth career double-double. Michigan's defense held Iowa to  35.6% shooting (21-of-59) from the field, including 6.3% (1-for-16) from three-point range. The win marked the Wolverines ninth consecutive win in the [[Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament]], setting a tournament record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401120736|title=Simpson directs No. 10 Michigan to 74–53 win over Iowa|access-date=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/15/mens-basketball-michigan-fires-on-all-cylinders-in-big-ten-tournament-quarterfinal-win-over-iowa.aspx|title=Michigan Fires on All Cylinders in Big Ten tournament Quarterfinal Win Over Iowa|access-date=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=McIntosh, Megan}}</ref>

The next day Michigan defeated Minnesota 76–49 in the semifinals of the Big Ten tournament, as Michigan shot 51.6% (32-of-62) from the field. Michigan was led by Livers with a career-high 21 points, while Simpson added 15 points and a game-high nine assists, and Brazdeikis added 13 points. With the win, Michigan advanced to the Big Ten tournament final for the third consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401120738|title=Livers scores 21, No. 10 Michigan pounds Minnesota 76–49|access-date=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/16/mens-basketball-wolverines-dominate-gophers-advance-to-big-ten-tournament-title-game.aspx|title=Wolverines Dominate Gophers, Advance to Big Ten tournament Title Game|access-date=March 16, 2019|date=March 16, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref> With nine assists in the game, Simpson became the 10th Wolverine to surpass 400 career assists. The win marked Beilein's 20th Big Ten tournament victory, becoming the third coach in tournament history to reach the milestone.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/17/mens-basketball-wolverines-face-spartans-for-big-ten-tournament-title-in-chicago.aspx|title=Wolverines Face Spartans for Big Ten tournament Title in Chicago|access-date=March 17, 2019|date=March 17, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref>

On March 17, Michigan lost to Michigan State 65–60 in the finals of the Big Ten tournament. Michigan was led by Brazdeikis with 19 points, while Poole added 13 points, and Teske added 10 points and 10 rebounds for his second double-double of the tournament. Michigan led by as many as 13 points early in the second half, but Michigan State went on a 13–4 run to tie the game at 48 with just over seven minutes remaining. The Spartans finished the game on a 10–0 run in the final two minutes of the game to secure the victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401120739|title=McQuaid, Winston lead Michigan over Michigan State 65–60|access-date=March 17, 2019|date=March 17, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/17/mens-basketball-michigan-falls-to-msu-in-big-ten-tournament-championship-game.aspx|title=Michigan Falls to MSU in Big Ten tournament championship Game|access-date=March 17, 2019|date=March 17, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref> The loss snapped Michigan's record-setting 10 game Big Ten tournament winning streak. Simpson finished the tournament with a tournament-record 30 assists in three games, surpassing the previous record of 29 assists set by [[Mateen Cleaves]] in [[1999 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|1999]]. Brazdeikis and Simpson were both named to the All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/documents/2019/3/17//MSU_Michigan_notes.pdf?id=6394|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190321211016/https://bigten.org/documents/2019/3/17//MSU_Michigan_notes.pdf?id=6394|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 21, 2019|title=2019 Big Ten Men's Basketball Tournament Game 13 Game Notes|access-date=March 18, 2019|date=March 17, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=BigTen.org}}</ref>

===NCAA tournament===
On March 21, Michigan began their participation in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]] with a 74–55 victory over [[2018–19 Montana Grizzlies basketball team|Montana]] in the first round for the second consecutive year. Michigan was led by Matthews with a game-high 22 points and 10 rebounds, for his seventh career double-double, while Brazdeikis added 14 points, Teske added 11 points and nine rebounds, and Poole added 10 points. Simpson posted 10 assists in the game for the eighth time this season, setting a single-season program record for the most games with 10 or more assists. Michigan's defense held the Grizzlies to 33.3% shooting, while forcing 10 turnovers, as Montana missed 13 of its first 16 shots in the first half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123405|title=Matthews' double-double leads Michigan past Grizzlies, 74–53|access-date=March 22, 2019|date=March 22, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/21/mens-basketball-michigan-marches-on-after-rolling-past-montana-in-ncaa-tournament.aspx|title=Michigan Marches on After Rolling Past Montana in NCAA tournament|access-date=March 22, 2019|date=March 22, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref>

On March 23, Michigan defeated [[2018–19 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] 64–49 in the second round. Michigan was led by Poole with a game-high 19 points, including four three-pointers, while Simpson added nine points, nine rebounds and nine assists, one point, rebound and assist shy of his second career triple-double. Michigan's defense held Florida to 34.5% shooting for the game, including 28.6% shooting in the second half, while their 49 points was a season-low for the Gators. With the win, Michigan advanced to the Sweet 16 for the third consecutive season, and earned their fifth 30-win season in program history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123421|title=Michigan returning to Sweet 16 after toppling Florida 64–49|access-date=March 23, 2019|date=March 23, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/23/mens-basketball-wolverines-sweet-16-bound-with-win-over-florida.aspx|title=Wolverines Sweet 16 Bound with Win over Florida|access-date=March 23, 2019|date=March 23, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref>

On March 28, Michigan lost to (#9/#10) [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]] 63–44 in the Sweet Sixteen, as only five players scored for the Wolverines. Michigan was led by Brazdeikis with 17 points and a career-high 13 rebounds, for his third career double-double, while Matthews added 12 points. The Raiders defense held Michigan to just 16 field goals, 32% shooting and only a single three-point basket on 19 attempts, with the lone three-pointer coming from C.J. Baird. The Wolverines finished the season with a 30–7 record, for its second consecutive 30-win season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401123385|title=D up: Texas Tech clamps down in 63–44 win over Michigan|access-date=March 29, 2019|date=March 29, 2019|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2019/3/28/mens-basketball-michigans-season-comes-to-end-in-sweet-16-loss-to-texas-tech.aspx|title=Michigan's Season Comes to End in Sweet 16 Loss to Texas Tech|access-date=March 29, 2019|date=March 28, 2019|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|author=Wywrot, Tom}}</ref>
